summary: Jacqueline I. Stone is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at San Francisco State University (~1970–1974) and UCLA (~1983–1990), and was a professor at Princeton University (~1990–2020).
Jacqueline Kracker completed her PhD at the University of Tennessee (~2000–2006), where she studied with committee member Miriam Levering.

Jacqueline Suthren Hirst specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied under doctoral supervisor Julius Lipner (~1988–1993) and held a post at the University of Manchester (~1990–2004).
Jacques Bacot was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Paris (~1936–1954) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1936–1954).

Jacques Gernet was a sinologist and historian who studied at the University of Algiers 1 and the ENLOV. His posts included the CNRS, EHESS, Sorbonne, Paris Diderot University (~1968–1975), and the Collège de France (1975–1992).

Jacques Giès was a specialist in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history who studied at Beaux-Arts de Paris and Paris-Sorbonne University (~-1994). He served as Chief Curator of Chinese Painting at the Musée Guimet (~1980–2011).

Jacques May was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He worked as chief editor at EFEO and Hōbōgirin (~1968–1981) and served as a professor at the University of Lausanne (~1974–1992).
Jacques P. Leider is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at INALCO (~1987–1998) and became a director at the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2001.

Jacques Scheuer works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Madeleine Biardeau and at Université catholique de Louvain, where he served as professor (~1977–2007), alongside a post at Facultés Loyola Paris.
Jadunath Sarkar was a historian who studied at Presidency University, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta (~1887–1892). He later held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1926–1928).
Jae-seong Kim is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (-1995) under the supervision of Yasunori Ejima and Masahiro Shimoda.

Jagdish Kashyap was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University (~1929–1932) and the University of Kelaniya (~1933–1935), later serving as Director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1951–1973).

Jake H. Davis works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Marlboro College, the University of Hawaii, and CUNY Graduate Center, and held posts at NYU (~2014–2017), Brown University, City College of New York, and Barre Center.

Jakob Wilhelm Hauer specialized in Indology and religious studies, studying at Oxford and the University of Tübingen under Richard von Garbe. He held academic posts at the University of Marburg (~1925–1927) and the University of Tübingen (1927–1945).

James A. Benn works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, SOAS under Timothy H. Barrett, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., later holding posts at Lewis & Clark, Arizona State, and McMaster University.

James A. Matisoff is a linguist who studied at Harvard University (~1954–1959) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1963–1967). He subsequently served on the faculty at UC Berkeley (~1970–2006).

James A. Santucci is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He served as a Professor of Religion at California State University and as Chair and Professor of Comparative Religion at California State University, Fullerton (~1970–2012).

James Atkinson was an Indologist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies who was educated at the University of Edinburgh. In 1818, he held a post as Assistant Persian Professor at Fort William College.

James B. Apple is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1994, studying with John D. Dunne and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, among others.

James Blumenthal studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and at CIHTS. Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he held posts at Oregon State University (~2001–2014) and Maitripa College (~2005–2014).
